course.name: COMP4348 COMP5348 Enterprise Scale Software Architecture

rubric.long_description: A table of at least six operations, including app publication, app update, app purchase and retrieval of a user's purchased apps, with resource-oriented URIs.

ratings.long_description: At least six operations including the four required ones; URIs identify resources rather than actions; resource, URI and verb given for each operation.
A required operation missing, fewer than six operations, or a few action-style or inconsistent URIs.
An RPC-style design with actions in the URIs, or two or more of the required operations missing.

rubric.description: Q1(b) HTTP verbs and success status codes
rubric.long_description: An appropriate HTTP verb and one success status code for each operation.

ratings.long_description: Verbs and status codes appropriate for every operation.
One inappropriate verb or status code.
Two or more inappropriate verbs or status codes, or status codes missing.

rubric.description: Q2(1) Service demands and low-load bounds
rubric.long_description: Service demand at each device for the given transaction mix, and the low-load throughput and response-time bounds, with working shown.

ratings.long_description: Device demands and both bounds correct, with working.
Correct method with an arithmetic or unit error.
Bounds not derived from service demands, or no working.

rubric.long_description: The high-load response-time bound used to find the largest number of clients for which the bound stays below 2 seconds, and the bottleneck device identified. Errors carried forward from earlier parts are not penalised again.

ratings.long_description: Correct bottleneck and correct largest integer, with working.
Correct method, but the wrong integer or the bottleneck not stated.
Bound not based on the bottleneck demand, or wrong bottleneck.

rubric.long_description: Service demands that depend on N, the largest N for which the high-load bound stays below 2 seconds, and the bottleneck throughput bound at that N. Errors carried forward from earlier parts are not penalised again.

ratings.long_description: N-dependent demands, correct N and correct throughput bound, with working.
N-dependent demands used, but N or the throughput bound wrong or missing.
Update mix treated as fixed, or no N-dependent demands.

rubric.description: Q2(4) CPU upgrade and new bottleneck
rubric.long_description: The smallest speed-up beyond which CPU upgrades no longer improve the throughput bound, the device that then limits throughput, and the maximum throughput bound reachable through CPU upgrades alone. Errors carried forward from earlier parts are not penalised again.

ratings.long_description: All three results correct and derived from the service demands.
Two of the three results correct.
One or none correct, or results not derived from the service demands.

rubric.long_description: The availability of each component and of the series system, with working.

ratings.long_description: Component and system availability correct, combined correctly for components in series.
Correct method with an arithmetic or unit error.
Series availability not combined correctly.

rubric.long_description: The MTTF and MTTR of the series system, with working. Errors carried forward from earlier parts are not penalised again.

ratings.long_description: MTTF and MTTR both correct, using a valid method.
Only one of MTTF or MTTR correct.
Neither correct.

rubric.long_description: The availability of the redundant 2-plex, treating one complete StoreSys as the replicated unit. Errors carried forward from earlier parts are not penalised again.

ratings.long_description: Parallel availability correct, applied to the whole StoreSys.
Correct method with an arithmetic error, or redundancy applied per component.
Availability not combined as a parallel system.

rubric.long_description: The MTTF of the 2-plex using the n-plex approximation, and its MTTR, with working. Errors carried forward from earlier parts are not penalised again.

ratings.long_description: MTTF from the n-plex approximation and MTTR from a valid method, both correct.
Only one of MTTF or MTTR correct.
Neither MTTF nor MTTR correct.
